title: IDF Kills Hamas Nahal Oz Commander Hamza Sharbasi and Azzam Al-Hayya (Son of Chief Negotiator) in Gaza Strike
detail: An Israeli airstrike in the Shejaiya neighborhood of Gaza City on May 13, 2026 killed Hamza Sharbasi, a commander in Hamas's Shejaiya Battalion who participated in the October 7, 2023 raid on the Nahal Oz military base. The same strike also killed Azzam al-Hayya, the 23-year-old son of Hamas chief negotiator Khalil al-Hayya. Azzam's death marks at least the second son of Khalil al-Hayya killed by Israeli strikes since the October 2025 ceasefire — a previous son was killed on May 8. IDF said both targets were armed operatives; the simultaneous killing of the Hamas negotiator's son is seen as a calculated pressure tactic against disarmament talks, which have been deadlocked since late April. Hamas condemned the strike as 'targeting the families of our leadership to break Palestinian resolve.' The strike further complicated the Board of Peace-mediated negotiations over Hamas disarmament.

media.caption: IDF kills Hamas Shejaiya Battalion commander Hamza Sharbasi and Azzam al-Hayya (son of Hamas negotiator Khalil al-Hayya) in Gaza airstrike — May 13, 2026

title: Settler Riot in Jaljilya: IDF Kills One Palestinian After Altercation Over Stolen Sheep
detail: Israeli settlers entered the Palestinian village of Jaljilya near Ramallah on May 13, 2026, searching for a stolen herd of sheep. Upon leaving, the encounter escalated into a violent riot involving stone-throwing. Israeli troops and Border Police responded with riot-dispersal measures and live fire, killing one Palestinian. The incident reflects the continuation of near-daily settler-Palestinian friction across the West Bank that has been documented since October 2023 — with settlers conducting incursions into Palestinian villages often under IDF protection, and IDF forces frequently used to respond to or enable settler confrontations. The UN documented 122 Palestinians killed by Israeli forces and settlers in April 2026 alone. IDF Central Command Chief Avi Bluth had publicly called settler violence 'Jewish terror' on May 1, but military responses to settler-triggered confrontations continue under existing rules of engagement.

media.caption: Settler riot in Jaljilya leads to IDF killing of one Palestinian; settlers had entered village searching for stolen sheep — Times of Israel, May 13, 2026

title: Netanyahu Coalition Pulls All Knesset Bills, Prepares Self-Dissolution to Control Election Timing
detail: The Netanyahu coalition on May 13, 2026 pulled all bills from the Knesset agenda amid concerns it lacks the votes to pass legislation following the Haredi draft exemption crisis. The coalition simultaneously began preparing to submit its own Knesset dissolution bill as early as the following week — a strategic move to control election timing rather than allowing opposition factions to force an earlier or less favorable dissolution. If the coalition's own dissolution bill passes, elections currently scheduled for October 27, 2026 could be moved up to late August or September. By controlling the dissolution process, Netanyahu's coalition aims to prevent a chaotic collapse and instead engineer a managed transition on its preferred timeline. The Haredi Degel HaTorah and Agudat Yisrael factions remain committed to supporting dissolution after Netanyahu shelved the military draft exemption bill. Channel 12 polling showed only 58% of 2022 Likud voters plan to vote Likud again, with 28% planning to switch parties. The coalition's fragility is compounded by ongoing judicial tensions after Justice Minister Levin threatened on May 7 to let the Supreme Court 'go extinct.'

media.caption: Netanyahu coalition pulls all bills from Knesset agenda and prepares self-dissolution bill to control election timing — Ynet News, May 13, 2026

title: Board of Peace 'Losing Patience' with Hamas; Mladenov Meets Netanyahu in Jerusalem
detail: US-backed Board of Peace High Representative Nickolay Mladenov met with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Jerusalem on May 13, 2026. Mladenov described the discussions as 'positive and substantive' and said both sides reaffirmed commitment to Trump's 20-point comprehensive Gaza peace plan. Haaretz reported that the Board of Peace is 'losing patience' with Hamas and is pushing the Trump plan forward without Hamas's explicit buy-in — a significant shift in the negotiating posture. Hamas has refused to discuss disarmament until Israel fully withdraws behind the October 2025 ceasefire 'Yellow Line'; Israel refuses to withdraw before Hamas disarms. The Board of Peace was established under the February 2026 Trump-Netanyahu framework and has been mediating disarmament talks in Qatar and Jerusalem. With Hamas disarmament talks formally stalled since late April, the Board is exploring whether the Trump plan's reconstruction and civilian governance provisions can proceed without a formal Hamas disarmament agreement. The IDF now controls approximately 59% of the Gaza Strip under the ceasefire framework.

media.caption: Board of Peace 'losing patience' with Hamas; Mladenov meets Netanyahu and pushes Trump plan forward without Hamas buy-in — Haaretz, May 13, 2026

title: ICC Appeals Chamber Rejects Israel's Jurisdictional Challenge 3–2; Israel Abandons Formal Defense of War Crime Charges
detail: The International Criminal Court's Appeals Chamber on or around May 13, 2026 rejected Israel's jurisdictional challenge to the admissibility of criminal proceedings against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former Defense Minister Yoav Gallant, by a 3–2 majority. The ruling affirms that the ICC has jurisdiction over the charges against Israeli leaders related to post-October 7 events in Gaza, including alleged starvation as a weapon of war and deliberate attacks on civilians. Israel separately abandoned its formal defense against the war crime charges — a significant procedural development that may accelerate proceedings. Active ICC arrest warrants remain in force for Netanyahu and Gallant (issued November 2024). The US imposed sanctions on ICC Prosecutor Karim Khan and nine ICC judges in February 2025, and Khan has been on indefinite leave since May 2025. The ruling is seen as a major setback for Israeli legal strategy and further constrains Netanyahu's international travel to the 124 ICC member states obligated to arrest him. Draft warrants for National Security Minister Ben-Gvir and Finance Minister Smotrich have been reportedly prepared but not yet filed.

media.caption: ICC Appeals Chamber rejects Israel's jurisdictional challenge 3-2; Israel abandons formal defense of war crime charges against Netanyahu and Gallant — Just Security
